recipes.name: Cranberry, Apple, and Fresh Ginger Chutney

steps.text: Bring cranberries, raisins, water, both sugars, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce the heat to low and simmer until berries start to pop, about 5 minutes. Add onion, apple, and celery; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture begins to thicken, 5 to 10 more minutes.
Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly, about 15 minutes. Cover and refrigerate until flavors fully develop, 8 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry, Apple, and Fresh Ginger Chutney
raw_recipe.description: This cranberry apple chutney with fresh ginger and raisins makes a delicious addition to your Thanksgiving table. It tastes great in turkey sandwiches, too!

video.description: This cranberry chutney has bite and isn’t as sweet as most cranberry sauces.

review.reviewBody: I made this according to the recipe and wouldn't change a thing. The onion and celery add complexity to the overall flavor which sets this cranberry condiment apart from similar recipes. Thank you for sharing this!

Made this last year for Thanksgiving, everyone loved it, even the kids. In place of water I used orange juice and added orange zest after cooking. Made a double batch today. Used canning jars and processed in water bath for 10 minutes. Now we can have it even after cranberry season.

A nice change from "your usual cranberry sauce". I found it works best with sweet white onions, and I cut the sugar in half, which came out just right for my taste. To reduce the "sharp" onion taste (if you are concerned about the onions), a little more work is required: start roasting the onions in about 1 teaspoon of oil first in the pot, then, when the onions are light golden brown, add the white sugar and lightly caramelize. Then add the water and the other ingredients as the original recipe calls for. That way, the onions release their full sweetness, while the edge is taken off. I also think, adding about 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon of ground coriander would spice it up a bit, but I have not tried that yet myself.

Very good, but it was too sweet and a little bland for me. The second time I made it, I cut the sugar by half, added the juice of one orange and a tablespoon of orange zest. I also added cardamom powder, a pinch of mace and a pinch of cayenne pepper to the cranberries as they cooked down. I preferred it this way, but it is an individual thing. Thank you for the base recipe!

Love this recipe! I did add a star anise pod and 1/4 teaspoon garam masala for a more complex flavor, along with a diced jalapeno for some heat. My family loves this! Pour some on a block of cream cheese or a brie, makes a great appetizer.

This is a great recipe. The first time I made it exactly as written, and we enjoyed it immensely. It was just a little too sweet for it to be perfect though. The next time I cut the sugar down to 1/3 cup, and 1/2 cup brown sugar. I also made a little change to the water. I used 7/8 cup water and 1/8 cup spiced rum; sensational. This has now become a staple, and we don't wait for a holiday to make it. Even my cranberry hating son loves this dish. Thanks for the recipe!

We have used this recipe for several years, for holiday potlucks, you name it. We always treble the recipe because everyone wants to take some home. We largely follow the recipe. For raisins, we have found we like golden raisins the best, and we use white onion. We typically add a little extra ginger and cinnamon. Because we cook so much at once, for us it usually takes about an hour, and we always cook it a day or two in advance because it gets better with time. Thanks for an amazing recipe!

I made this today, with the thought of using it instead of traditional cranberry sauce. I love it! This recipe is a winner. Update: Since I wrote this review almost one year ago, I have found that this chutney enhances the flavors of any meat. Add it to a cracker or toast with any spreadable cheese, and it makes a tasty appetizer. Adding my favorite hot sauce to it gives it an entirely new and wonderful dimension. I have halved the amount of onion and celery and used it atop a whole cheesecake, to add beauty and flavor. It's great warmed and served over ice cream, or as a crepe filling with Nutella and whipped cream. Thank you for sharing this versatile and delicious recipe. I look forward to continuing to enjoy it for years to come.
Added a little more vinegar. Otherwise followed recipe. Then put in small canning jars and processed it in a water bath 30 minutes. Everyone who tries it loves it.

I have made this for the past 3 Thanksgivings. Was just trying to add something new to the mix. Am I glad I did! This was made exactly as written. Absolutely delicious . Nice balance of flavors. Had purchased a nice creamy gorgonzola cheese last night, made the chutney this morning. Toasted up some baguette today with a smear the gorgonzola and a dollop of the chutney! It was a big hit! Think I'm going to end up making a new batch for Thanksgiving. Thank you Foodelicious

The aroma was delicious as it simmered! Kept going over to stir it just because of it's smell : ) I served this with brie and crackers for an appetizer. Also substituted the water for orange juice and added 1/4 c chopped pecans.

I have made this one every year for quite a while now. So convenient to make ahead a week or a few days. Mince the onion really well and use a little less if you prefer. I also make another recipe with blueberries and raspberries for variety. Love this recipe! Thankyou
Made it vs regular cranberry sauce to go with the turkey…game changer. We also used in melted cheese sandwiches, and as a jam. Very versatile.
I made a double batch, thankfully. The flavors blend perfectly. I used a masher at the end to even out the consistency. Super easy to make in a short period of time.
I love this and make it every time I cook turkey. It’s great as a spread on turkey leftover sandwiches.

I made as written. I don’t know if my onions were on steroids or what, but I found it to have an overwhelm ing onion taste and after taste, and I like onions!. (I double checked the recipe and I had the measurments correct) It will be sort of ok for eating with strong meats, but I have more cranberries so will make another batch without the onions, so it will be ready by dinner time.
Made this for Thanksgiving and was a BIG hit. Made no changes.

Great flavors! Tart cranberry, sweet raisins and love the crunch of the apple and celery! However, next time I will omit the onion ... for me, that flavor didn't seem to go as well with the other flavors. But this is definitely going to be a staple on my holiday table!
I use this recipe to make cranberry sauce at Thanksgiving. I just omit the celery and onion and keep everything else the same. It's so good and the best cranberry sauce recipe I've ever found.
Added a HOTTT!!!1 Pepper powder and a pinch of cajun spice!!!1 = MAGNIFIQUE!!!1
